adjudication.rationale:
In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` the fallback path is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the `:` branch), the `.find(...)` predicate compares `cal.externalId` to that same falsy value (`undefined`/`null`), so it will almost never match any real calendar externalId. That turns what used to be a fallback to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId` into `undefined`, causing `events.update` to run against an undefined/incorrect `calendarId`. The same faulty pattern is also introduced in `deleteEvent` (`calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`). This is a concrete behavior regression visible from the diff.
